system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Milan, Italy. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Milan itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Milan space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Porta Venezia, Brera/Centro, Isola/Farini, Lambrate/Ventura, Tortona/Navigli, Città Studi/Bicocca) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Milan spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Milan, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Massimo De Carlo
galleries.address_hint: Viale Lombardia 17 (Casa Corbellini-Wassermann); also Palazzo Belgioioso
galleries.note: Italy's most internationally powerful gallery, with London/Hong Kong/Paris outposts; roster from Paola Pivi and Rudolf Stingel to Yan Pei-Ming, and a landmark Portaluppi-designed Milan space.

galleries.name: Galleria Lia Rumma
galleries.note: Historic Arte Povera-era dealer (founded Naples 1971) whose Milan warehouse shows Kentridge, Kounellis, Marina Abramović, Anselm Kiefer; constant museum crossover.

galleries.name: kaufmann repetto
galleries.note: Milan–New York gallery with a sharply feminist, research-driven programme (Pae White, Latifa Echakhch, Eva Rothschild, Nathalie Du Pasquier); fixture at Basel and Frieze.

galleries.name: Galleria Raffaella Cortese
galleries.note: Multi-space gallery known for major women artists — Ana Mendieta estate, Barbara Bloom, Zoe Leonard, Marcello Maloberti — and for launching Milan's Via Stradella cluster.

galleries.name: Pirelli HangarBicocca
galleries.note: Free-admission industrial kunsthalle housing Kiefer's 'Sette Palazzi Celesti'; its large-scale monographs set the international benchmark for Milan's contemporary scene.

galleries.name: Fondazione Prada
galleries.note: OMA-designed campus (plus Osservatorio in the Galleria) whose ambitious exhibitions and commissions made Milan a compulsory stop on the global art circuit.

galleries.name: Galleria Christian Stein
galleries.note: Founded 1966; the defining gallery of Arte Povera (Boetti, Merz, Pistoletto, Zorio) still pairing historic estates with younger Italians.

galleries.name: Gió Marconi
galleries.note: Heir to Studio Marconi, with a design-inflected international programme (Nathalie Djurberg & Hans Berg, John Bock, Judith Hopf) and steady fair presence.

galleries.name: Francesca Minini
galleries.note: Anchor of the Ventura Lambrate district; conceptual and post-minimal programme (Riccardo Beretta, Christian Frosi, Esther Kläs) with strong critical following.

galleries.name: ZERO...
galleries.note: Paolo Zani's gallery, a key exporter of a Milanese conceptual generation (Diego Perrone, Francesco Gennari, Alek O.) and a fixture of Art Basel Statements alumni.

galleries.name: Galleria Continua
galleries.note: Milan outpost of the San Gimignano-born global gallery; blue-chip international roster (Kapoor, JR, Ai Weiwei) in a central palazzo.

galleries.name: Studio Guenzani
galleries.note: Open since 1985, the gallery that brought Cindy Sherman, Nan Goldin, Vanessa Beecroft and Stefano Arienti to Milanese audiences.

galleries.name: Fondazione Nicola Trussardi
galleries.note: Massimiliano Gioni's roving foundation stages ambitious commissions in historic Milanese buildings; among Europe's most influential non-collecting institutions.

galleries.name: Monica De Cardenas
galleries.note: Since 1992 a rigorous painting/photography programme (Alex Katz, Thomas Ruff, Stephan Balkenhol), with satellites in Zuoz and Lugano.

galleries.name: Ordet
galleries.note: Edoardo Bonaspetti's non-profit space; curatorially precise shows and commissions that have become the critical barometer of young Milan.

galleries.name: Federico Vavassori
galleries.note: Small but internationally watched gallery of a new generation, showing artists such as Ha Chong-Hyun's peers and emerging figures picked up by museums abroad.

galleries.name: CLIMA
galleries.note: Matteo Consonni's gallery, a leading Milan discovery platform for young Italian and international artists; regular in emerging sections of major fairs.

galleries.name: ICA Milano
galleries.note: Non-profit institute opened 2019 in a former factory; solo shows, residencies and publications that fill Milan's kunsthalle gap.

galleries.name: Fondazione Carriero
galleries.note: Exhibitions of exceptional scholarly quality in a 17th-century palazzo, pairing historic figures (Fontana, Melotti) with contemporary interventions.

galleries.name: FANTA-MLN
galleries.note: Young gallery with an experimental, internationally networked programme; a regular presence in the emerging sections of Milan and European fairs.

galleries.name: Building
galleries.note: Multi-floor gallery with museum-standard installations and catalogues bridging postwar Italian masters and living artists.

galleries.name: Cardi Gallery
galleries.note: Milan–London dealer of postwar and contemporary blue chip (Burri, Schifano, Kusama, Ryan Sullivan) with scholarly historical surveys.

galleries.name: Prometeo Gallery Ida Pisani
galleries.note: Politically engaged programme (Regina José Galindo, Zhang Huan, Santiago Sierra) with strong biennial and institutional traction.

galleries.name: Renata Fabbri
galleries.note: Focused programme of emerging and mid-career artists, often women, with growing museum and fair visibility.

galleries.name: Galleria Poggiali
galleries.note: Florence-founded gallery whose Milan space mixes established Italians and international names in ambitious, well-produced shows.

galleries.name: Tommaso Calabro
galleries.note: Apartment-style palazzo gallery praised for research shows on Italian modernism (Dalí, Melotti, Leonor Fini) alongside contemporary interventions.

galleries.name: Ciaccia Levi
galleries.note: Paris–Milan gallery formed by Alessandro Ciaccia and Antoine Levi; forward-looking international roster and consistent fair presence.

galleries.name: Vistamare
galleries.note: Pescara-born gallery with a Milan space; refined conceptual programme (Marisa Merz legacy, Alessandro Piangiamore, international photography).

galleries.name: Fondazione Mudima
galleries.note: Founded 1989 by Gino Di Maggio; the key Italian home for Fluxus, Gutai and Nouveau Réalisme, with a vast archive and exhibition programme.

galleries.name: Galleria Milano
galleries.note: Active since 1928 and run by the Bonomo/Cardazzo lineage of Milanese dealing; historic conceptual archive plus contemporary shows.

galleries.name: A arte Invernizzi
galleries.note: Authority on analytical painting and European minimal-concrete art (Nicola Carrino, Rodolfo Aricò, Günter Umberg), with a serious publishing arm.

galleries.name: Eduardo Secci
galleries.note: Florence-based gallery whose Milan space shows an international mid-career roster; active at Artissima, miart and Basel satellites.

galleries.name: Spazio Maiocchi
galleries.note: Kaleidoscope-run venue where art, fashion and music converge; commissions and Milan Art Week events with a large international audience.

galleries.name: Marsèll Paradise
galleries.note: Non-commercial space backed by the Marsèll label, offering carefully curated solo projects by emerging artists.

galleries.name: Fondazione Sozzani
galleries.note: Carla Sozzani's gallery-turned-foundation, a historic Milan address for photography and image culture since 1990.

galleries.name: Fondazione Adolfo Pini
galleries.note: Historic house-foundation with a sharp contemporary programme, residencies and curatorial commissions.

galleries.name: Fondazione Converso
galleries.note: Baroque deconsecrated church hosting site-specific projects by significant international artists; one of Milan's most atmospheric venues.

galleries.name: Fondazione Elpis
galleries.note: Marina Nissim's foundation, opened 2022, supporting young artists through exhibitions, prizes and residency projects.

galleries.name: Careof
galleries.address_hint: Fabbrica del Vapore, Via Giulio Cesare Procaccini 4
galleries.note: Since 1987 a key non-profit for emerging Italian art, with a major video and documentation archive.

galleries.name: Viafarini
galleries.address_hint: Fabbrica del Vapore, Via Giulio Cesare Procaccini 4
galleries.note: Founded 1991; artist archive, open studios and residencies that have supported generations of Milanese artists.

galleries.name: Casa degli Artisti
galleries.note: Legendary Brera artists' house relaunched in 2019 as a public residency and exhibition centre.

galleries.name: Assab One
galleries.note: Former printing works run by Elena Quarestani; ambitious, free exhibitions and long-running support for site-responsive projects.

galleries.name: Fondazione Arnaldo Pomodoro
galleries.note: Artist's foundation with sculpture-focused research exhibitions, a prize for young sculptors and a major archive.

galleries.name: Fondazione Stelline
galleries.note: Central exhibition palazzo with a busy programme of contemporary art and photography surveys.

galleries.name: Galleria Fumagalli
galleries.note: Founded in Bergamo in 1991 and Milan-based since 2015; conceptual and performance legacies (Chris Burden, Marina Abramović circle).

galleries.name: Antonio Colombo Arte Contemporanea
galleries.note: Long-running gallery bridging figurative painting, illustration and pop-surrealism, with a strong Milanese following.

galleries.name: Galleria Bianconi
galleries.note: Painting-centred programme combining Italian postwar rediscoveries with contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Otto Zoo
galleries.note: Independent-minded gallery with a photographic and conceptual bias; consistent quality since 2010.

galleries.name: Ribot
galleries.note: International emerging-to-mid-career programme with a notable Nordic and German axis.

galleries.name: Ncontemporary
galleries.note: Milan gallery (formerly with London space) supporting young international artists and photography-based practices.

galleries.name: Galleria Suzy Shammah
galleries.note: Dealer with deep Milanese roots showing conceptual and photographic practices in tightly edited exhibitions.

galleries.name: Mimmo Scognamiglio Artecontemporanea
galleries.note: Naples-born dealer active in Milan, mixing international mid-career names with Italian postwar material.

galleries.name: Cassina Projects
galleries.note: Gallery with New York origins showing emerging international artists in a large industrial Milan space.

galleries.name: M77 Gallery
galleries.note: Large multi-level gallery alternating historical surveys of Italian art with contemporary solo shows.

galleries.name: The Flat – Massimo Carasi
galleries.note: Long-standing gallery for young international figuration and sculpture, active on the fair circuit since 1997.

galleries.name: Galleria Giovanni Bonelli
galleries.note: Painting-focused gallery bridging Italian postwar rediscoveries and contemporary artists; spaces also outside Milan.

galleries.name: Loom Gallery
galleries.note: Programme rooted in geometric abstraction and international minimal-conceptual traditions.

galleries.name: Dep Art Gallery
galleries.note: Specialist in kinetic, programmed and optical art (Alberto Biasi, Turi Simeti) with scholarly catalogues.

galleries.name: Galleria Gaburro
galleries.note: Verona-born gallery with a Milan space showing international painters and Italian mid-career artists.

galleries.name: Robilant+Voena
galleries.note: London–Milan–New York dealer combining old masters and modern with contemporary exhibitions of museum ambition.

galleries.name: Tornabuoni Arte
galleries.note: Major dealer in Italian postwar masters (Fontana, Burri, Boetti) with an international network and fair presence.

galleries.name: Cortesi Gallery
galleries.note: Milan–Lugano gallery focused on ZERO, Spatialism and postwar abstraction, with well-researched thematic shows.

galleries.name: Galleria Blu
galleries.note: Founded 1957, one of Milan's historic avant-garde galleries; a living archive of Italian and European postwar art.

galleries.name: Lorenzelli Arte
galleries.note: Family gallery active since the 1950s, specialising in abstraction and concrete art with occasional contemporary shows.

galleries.name: Galleria Tega
galleries.note: High-end dealer in modern and postwar Italian art staging polished exhibitions with contemporary counterpoints.

galleries.name: Pack
galleries.note: Central gallery with an eclectic contemporary programme of Italian and international artists.

galleries.name: Bianca Maria Rizzi & Matthias Ritter
galleries.note: Italo-German gallery with a rigorous programme of conceptual and photographic practices.

galleries.name: Antonio Battaglia Arte Contemporanea
galleries.note: Small Brera gallery known for consistent support of Italian abstraction and younger painters.

galleries.name: Marcorossi artecontemporanea
galleries.note: Established gallery with spaces in several Italian cities, showing recognised Italian contemporary painters and sculptors.

galleries.name: Dimora Artica
galleries.note: Artist-run apartment space with an inventive curatorial programme and a role in Milan's independent network.

galleries.name: The Open Box
galleries.note: Independent space supporting experimental projects, publishing and performance in Isola.

galleries.name: Tile Project Space
galleries.note: Non-profit project space known for sound, performance and research-based exhibitions by young artists.

galleries.name: GLUCK50
galleries.note: Residency and exhibition space hosting international artists and curators for Milan-focused projects.

galleries.name: Isola Art Center
galleries.note: Emblematic activist art platform born from the Isola neighbourhood struggles; internationally cited model of art and urban politics.

galleries.name: FM Centro per l'Arte Contemporanea
galleries.address_hint: Via Gaudenzio Ferrari / Via Piranesi 10 (Frigoriferi Milanesi)
galleries.note: Exhibition centre known for large surveys of private collections and Italian contemporary art.

galleries.name: BASE Milano
galleries.note: Ex-Ansaldo cultural hub with residencies, exhibitions and a central role during Milan Art Week and Design Week.

galleries.name: Galleria San Fedele
galleries.note: Jesuit-run gallery whose long-standing prize and exhibitions have supported young Italian artists for decades.

galleries.name: Officine Saffi
galleries.note: Gallery, residency and award devoted to contemporary ceramics, with international recognition in the field.

galleries.name: 29 Arts in Progress
galleries.note: Photography gallery handling major fashion and reportage names, active at photo fairs internationally.

galleries.name: MC2 Gallery
galleries.note: Photography-focused gallery representing international documentary and staged photographers.

galleries.name: Podbielski Contemporary
galleries.note: Berlin-born gallery now in Milan, showing photography and conceptual work with a strong female roster.

galleries.name: Wunderkammern
galleries.note: Rome-founded gallery with a Milan space specialising in urban and post-graffiti art with international names.

galleries.name: Nuova Galleria Morone
galleries.note: Central gallery with a programme of contemporary painting, sculpture and works on paper.

galleries.name: Ca' di Fra'
galleries.note: Long-established gallery combining Italian postwar figures with contemporary Italian artists.

galleries.name: Artopia Gallery
galleries.note: Rita Urso's gallery, active for decades with a conceptual and politically aware Italian programme.

galleries.name: Fondazione Corrente
galleries.note: Ernesto Treccani's foundation, an archive and exhibition space linking Milan's 20th-century legacy to contemporary practice.
